# Under the Hood

Source: https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/internals.html

REFERENCE

# Under the Hood

How the simulator actually works: the Rust and Python split, the three layers of the price model, the book, the macro chain, the random number architecture, and why the determinism guarantee holds to the last bit.

## Rust Core, Python API

Everything that runs a market lives in the Rust crate: the engine, the price model, the order book, the economy, the RNG and the vendored maths. The Python package re-exports it and adds the parts better written in Python: JSON round-trips, process pools for seed sweeps, and the analysis modules (facts, loss, envelope, atlas, tca). Forcing those into the extension would mean hand-rolling JSON escaping and reimplementing a process pool, both worse than the standard library versions.

## Where a Decision Lives

The day loop now lives in the core: the macro step, the day close, and the mapping of initial state. Previously parts of it sat in the bindings, which meant the browser surface and the Python surface each ran their own copy.

The rule behind that move is worth stating, because it is what keeps two surfaces honest: if it decides something about the market, it belongs in the core. A binding that re-implements a modelling decision is a fork wearing the costume of glue code, and the divergence stays invisible until a whole simulated market has drifted.

## How a Price Is Built

Factorsone normal, one uniformPrices-process, then breakerVolumespends phase 1's uniformSettlementthe book printsthenthenthen

the uniform is stashed, not used

the breaker runs again, on the print

one tick, per company

The order of operations is the model. The uniform drawn
in phase 1 is not used there; it is consumed in phase 3, so a port that
drew it where it is used would produce identical draw counts and a
different stream. The circuit breaker is applied twice, and the second
application is the one that matters, because the settled print becomes
the next tick's reference.

Layer 1: fair value from fundamentals. Each instrument gets a true value computed from its fundamentals, discounted at the prevailing rates. This anchor moves: when the central bank's meeting calendar moves the discount rate, fair value reprices per instrument. The one exception is a loss-maker valued off book value, which carries no discount rate.

Layer 2: an autoregressive mispricing process. The market price wanders around fair value through a mispricing term with mean reversion, momentum and a herding component, plus news shocks. This wedge between price and value is the ground truth the truth table records, and its momentum term is what makes returns trend. Under pt-v1 that reads +0.249 at lag one against a real band around zero; the shipped pt-v12 turns the term down to 0.0186 and measures +0.0239, inside the band. The herding term is load-bearing for the model's identity, and the counterfactual is one line: ModelParams.from_preset("pt-v1", momentum_theta=0.05) measured in band, honestly fingerprinted as custom.

Layer 3: GJR-GARCH volatility with a shared market factor. Every name runs a GJR-GARCH variance process, so volatility clusters and reacts asymmetrically to losses, which is where the leverage effect comes from: a symmetric process produces none at any coefficients. On top sits a shared market factor with its own conditional variance, coupled to VIX. The factor's variance reverts to a target scaling with (VIX/15)², so a pinned VIX moves realised volatility: 31% annualised at VIX 5, 37% at 15, 105% at 45, 126% at 65. Above VIX 25.5 the cross-section blends toward the factor, and mean pairwise correlation reads +0.20 calm, +0.62 at VIX 45, +0.68 at 65. Diversification fails under stress the way real crises make it fail. Since the 2026-08-26 era boundary the coupling is not the factor's alone: a name's own GJR-GARCH variance follows the VIX too (garch_vix_coupling 0.3), the sector draw's variance follows the regime in full (sector_vix_coupling 1.0, which was a quarter under pt-v10 and was quadrupled by pt-v11's crisis work), the VIX's own fear channel reads the day's index return rather than the closing minute, the volatility regimes come off the market instead of the business cycle, and the factor's variance clamp sits at 32x its baseline rather than 8x. Descriptions of these mechanics written for pt-v3 do not carry over. Universe.random(20-25, seed=11) · 120 days · sim seed 3, VIX pinned. Those levels straddle the certified panel's 32.76% rather than sitting near it, the two calm pins bracketing it and the two crisis pins running three to four times higher, because a pinned VIX is not a normal market: the pin drives the factor variance directly, and these runs use a smaller roster over 120 days rather than the certified 40 names over 252. The ratio between two of them is also not the crisis lever the realism page quotes, which is measured on the certified roster. Compare pins against each other, and take a headline volatility number from an unpinned run. See Realism and Limits.

## The Order Book

Matching runs against a limit order book with price-time priority. You get queue position, partial fills, and a quoted spread that widens under stress. Impact is emergent: a large order pays worse prices because it consumed levels, and there is no slippage coefficient anywhere in the code. Read that as a statement about the mechanism, not about calibration: the realism envelope measures daily price, correlation and volume statistics, and nothing in it grades depth shape, cancellation intensity, queue dynamics, the intraday spread distribution, impact decay, resiliency or order-sign autocorrelation against real market data. The book is real and it is not certified. Session circuit breakers halt a name when a move binds the breaker, and the golden tests pin that behaviour tick by tick. The measured cost of trading too often is in Running a market.

## The Macro Chain

A full Taylor/Phillips/Okun loop advances at every day close: economy update, cycle transition, central bank. VIX takes a new value every day. The policy fields step at the central bank's meeting calendar: over one measured 120-day run, the funds rate took 2 distinct values, the corporate bond yield 3, inflation 4, GDP growth 6, and fair value repriced per instrument on the meeting days the discount rate moved, days 45 and 96 of that run. A pin overrides the endogenous step from the day it lands. Universe.random(20, seed=11) · sim seed 42 · run_days(120)

## RNG Streams

One seed drives the whole simulation, through seven independent substreams, so changing what one consumer draws cannot shift any other consumer's sequence. Four of the seven exist because of that rule rather than in spite of it: a mechanism that consumes draws could not have been added to a shared stream at all without shifting every later draw and moving every shipped preset's trajectory, so jumps, volume, news and per-name volume each got a stream of their own and each arrived inert.

StreamIdServes

market0every draw in the tick: market factor, sector factors, per-company noise, volume, book settlement
economy1the daily macro chain: economy update, cycle transition, central bank
external2the embedder, through Engine.draw_uniform() / draw_normal()
jumps3endogenous jumps, drawn once per name per day at the close
volume4the common persistent volume component, drawn once per day at the close
news5endogenous company news, drawn once per name per day at the open
volume_idio6per-name volume persistence, drawn once per name per day

Why the split exists. TCA re-runs the market without your orders, and the subtraction is exact only if the untraded world sees the identical noise. The macro chain's draw count genuinely varies with macro state: a chain in contraction rolls a shock the expansion never draws, so it needs its own stream. And a host application that takes one random number of its own must never invalidate a seeded market. The market stream's schedule is a pure function of market status, active roster and sector count, so no price, no macro value and no order flow can move its position. Engine.draws_by_stream() reports the counts for the first three, which are the ones a TCA subtraction compares; the four later streams are diagnosed through the snapshot instead, where each occupies three of the 21 numbers in state_snapshot()["rng"].

The derivation is a contract, pinned by a golden test against hand-computed values:

DERIVATION
Copy

```
mixed = splitmix64_mix((s > 32 # top 32 bits
sequence_k = 256 + k
stream_k = GameRng(seed_k, sequence_k) # PCG-XSH-RR 64/32
```

Two properties make the streams independent. Each stream gets its own PCG sequence, hence its own odd increment, and two PCG32 generators with different increments traverse different orbits: one can never be a time-shifted copy of the other, by construction. And the seed is passed through an avalanche mixer first, because seeding two streams with the same raw state leaves a deterministic cross-stream relation that the output permutation only obscures. The mixer gives every stream an unrelated starting state. Everything in the derivation is integer arithmetic, exactly specified on every platform, so it adds nothing for the bit-identity claim to trip on.

## Why the Crate Bans std Transcendentals

Rust's f64::cos delegates to the platform's maths library: MSVC's on Windows, glibc's on Linux, Apple's on macOS. They give different answers. Measured, one operation out of four differs:

OpRust std vs V8

lnidentical
sqrtidentical (IEEE-754 specifies it exactly)
sinidentical
cosdiffers by 1 ULP

One function, one bit, and one bit is enough. Normal draws route through cos, they feed the GARCH noise term for every company on every tick, and price = fair value × exp(s) is a non-linear feedback loop, so a last-bit difference becomes a different market within a simulated year. The same disagreement exists between browsers: measured across 60,000 recorded normal draws, Chrome's answers differ from a platform-libm build on 1.545% of draws, with the first divergence at draw 12. A parity test that checked six draws passed by stopping six short of the first mismatch. A test can pass because it is too small, and that is what it looks like.

So the crate vendors its maths: exp, log, pow, sin and cos come from the libm crate, a pure-Rust port of MUSL's implementation, the same code everywhere it compiles. No std transcendental reaches the source, and a test greps the source to enforce that rather than trusting anyone to remember.

What has been measured, by commit: identical digests on Windows x86_64 and macOS arm64 at a5afd1c; identical digests on all five targets (Linux x86_64 and aarch64, macOS arm64 and x86_64, Windows x86_64) at ad91026; the current era's baseline regenerated and confirmed on macOS arm64 only, until the gate runs again. The gate has not yet run against a tagged release. Read cross-platform bit-identity as measured at ad91026 and as engineering intent for the current baseline.

## Performance

A 252-day year over 100 instruments takes 27 seconds on the documentation's reference desktop and under seven on an Apple-silicon laptop. Recording 9.8 million rows of ground truth costs less than wall-clock timing resolves: measured as interleaved pairs of recorded and plain runs, nearly half the pairs come out negative. Sweeps parallelise 3 to 4 times on eight cores, and runs stream a batch per day, so a hundred-seed sweep at tick grain never has to fit in memory.

---


# The Nine Components

Source: https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/factors.html

REFERENCE

# The Nine Components

Every tick's change in mispricing is broken into nine components that sum to it. These are the names the truth table uses, the values explain_price_move returns, and the closed set an agent's explain must answer from. The crate calls them S_COMPONENT_KEYS; the runtime list is Engine.FACTORS.

## The Set

In order. The first three are the model’s own dynamics, the next four are shocks, and the last two are discrete events the engine books after the tick chain.

NameWhat it is

reversionThe pull back toward fair value. Mispricing decays at a rate set by its half-life, so this term is negative when a name is above fair value and positive when it is below.
momentumHerding: the fraction of yesterday's re-rating that continues today. Controlled by momentum_theta, and the reason returns trend here.
crowd_leanThe crowd's net flow. It net-buys what trades below fair value and net-sells what trades above, and it also chases yesterday's move. Bounded, so the crowd can never dominate a news day.
company_newsNews priced into this name: its own events at full weight, its sector's at a fraction, market-wide events at a smaller fraction, and a peer's event where peer transfer is switched on.
order_flow_impactThe permanent, information-bearing part of order imbalance. Your own orders land here. The temporary part is not in this column, because it shows up in the price the book settled rather than in the model's target.
short_squeeze_effectForced flow: short squeezes and stop cascades. Fires on high short interest into a rising price, and on cascades in either direction.
random_noiseThe idiosyncratic draw, scaled by the name's beta, its sector's volatility, its size, and the GARCH variance state.
circuit_breakerThe session circuit breaker’s own correction. When the model price leaves the allowed band the tick re-derives the state from the clamped price, and until 2026-08-26 that rewrite was booked to nobody, so on any day the breaker bound the columns did not reconstruct the move.
jumpThe daily jump, applied after the tick loop rather than inside it, and recorded on the tick where it is first observed. Every preset from pt-v4 carries jumps, and without this column those days never reconstructed.

## They Sum, and That Is the Point

Difference mispricing_s across two ticks, add the nine columns, and the residual should be around 1e-16. That is what makes this a dataset rather than a commentary: you can check a label against the outcome instead of trusting it.

PYTHON
Copy

```
import pretium as pt
import polars as pl

engine = pt.Engine(seed=42, universe=pt.Universe.random(20, seed=11))
engine.run_days(120) # long enough for a jump to fire
truth = pl.from_arrow(engine.truth())

FACTORS = ["reversion", "momentum", "crowd_lean", "company_news",
"order_flow_impact", "short_squeeze_effect", "random_noise",
"circuit_breaker", "jump"] # Engine.FACTORS

one = truth.filter(pl.col("instrument_id") == 0).sort("day", "tick")
delta = one["mispricing_s"].diff()
summed = one.select(sum(pl.col(c) for c in FACTORS)).to_series()
print((delta[1:] - summed[1:]).abs().max()) # ~1e-16
```

Run it over five days instead of 120 and the seven-column version of this check also passes, because five days is too short for a jump to fire. On this seed over 120 days, with 8 jump ticks, seven columns are off by 0.128 and nine by 6.75e-17. Where a residual does remain, the mispricing clamp bound; the circuit breaker has had its own column since 2026-08-26 and is no longer part of it.

Which is also a caveat on the older promise, and it is stated here rather than left for someone to rediscover. Before 2026-08-26 the identity held on every day neither mechanism fired and did not hold on the days they did: any day a jump landed, on any preset from pt-v4 onward, and any day the session circuit breaker bound, on any preset at all. So a ground-truth decomposition published from a 0.1.x release is exact except on those days, and the columns were never wrong, only incomplete. Both are columns now and the identity holds through a crisis.

Engine.FACTORS is the same list at runtime, so an agent can validate its own answer against it rather than hardcoding strings.

## Scope

It is not a decomposition of the price. It decomposes the mispricing, which is the gap between price and fair value. Everything that moves fair value itself, such as a rate change repricing the discount, is in fundamental_value instead.

And it is per tick, deliberately. A day-level attribution can say order flow moved a price today; it cannot say when, and a label you cannot align to a bar is not a label. A name that did not tick has zeros across all nine, because nothing contributed to a move it did not make.

Related: Tables and Schemas for the columns these sit in, and The Agent Harness for the explain contract that scores against them.

---


# Tables and Schemas

Source: https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/schemas.html

REFERENCE

# Tables and Schemas

Every column a run gives you, plus the enumerations the rest of the docs refer to.

## The Output Tables

All five read zero-copy into polars, pandas, pyarrow and duckdb, and the package depends on none of them. Every table keys its rows by instrument_id, which is the roster index, so roster order matters here as it does everywhere else.

## bars

OHLCV. grain="tick" gives close and volume per tick; grain="day" gives open, high, low, close and volume per bar.

ColumnType

dayuint32Day index.
tickuint32Tick index. A tick is a minute, and there are 390 in a day. Tick grain only.
baruint32Bar index within the day. Day grain only.
instrument_iduint32Roster index.
open · high · lowfloat64Day grain only.
closefloat64What the book actually settled.
volumefloat64Shares.

## truth

The answer key. Three levels plus the nine factor contributions.

ColumnType

day · tick · instrument_iduint32Keys.
mispricing_sfloat64Log gap between price and fair value.
fundamental_valuefloat64What the company is worth: earnings, growth, the sector anchor, rates. No mispricing in it.
anchor_pricefloat64fundamental_value * exp(mispricing_s): the price the model wanted before the book touched it. So close - anchor_price isolates microstructure, and mispricing_s isolates the valuation gap.
reversion · momentum · crowd_lean · company_news · order_flow_impact · short_squeeze_effect · random_noise · circuit_breaker · jumpfloat64The nine factors, in this order. They sum to the change in mispricing_s.

A name that did not tick has zeros across the nine and keeps its last two level values, because a valuation does not disappear when trading is quiet.

## macro

ColumnType

dayuint32Day index. The row carries the values the day traded under; the close then advances the chain.
vixfloat64Takes a new value every day.
federal_funds_ratefloat64Fractional: 0.025 is 2.5%. Steps at the central bank's meeting calendar.
corporate_bond_yieldfloat64What equities discount off.
inflation_rate · unemployment_rate · gdp_growthfloat64The Taylor/Phillips/Okun loop's state.
qe_pe_boostfloat64Valuation support from policy.
fear_greed_indexfloat64Sentiment level.
universe_stressfloat64Remembered stress. Ratchets up on a shock and decays over weeks, which is what keeps correlation elevated after an event.

## fills

ColumnType

day · step · tick · instrument_iduint32When and what. step is the run-wide decision index.
quantityfloat64Shares. Signed.
pricefloat64Average fill price.
worst_pricefloat64The worst level you reached. The distance from price is how far you walked the book.
notionalfloat64Traded value.

## book

ColumnType

day · tick · instrument_iduint32Keys.
sideuint32Bid or ask.
leveluint32Depth index from the touch.
price · sizefloat64The resting quote.

## Granularities

bars(grain=) takes "tick" or "day". Both also accept a day= filter, and tick grain accepts minutes= to aggregate into bars of that many minutes, which is where intraday grains come from.

## The Twelve Sectors

Universe.random assigns these round-robin, so a roster is as close to balanced as its size allows: 60 names give five each, and the certified 40 give four to four sectors and three to the other eight. You pass the key rather than the display name, with a typo refused rather than quietly routed to a generic default. Anchor P/E and daily sigma are what the sector contributes to valuation and to volatility.

KeyNameAnchor P/EVolDaily sigma

technologyTechnology32.01.20.025
financial_servicesFinancial Services12.01.10.015
healthcareHealthcare24.00.90.018
energyEnergy10.01.30.015
consumer_discretionaryConsumer Discretionary20.010.018
consumer_staplesConsumer Staples20.00.70.008
industrialsIndustrials17.010.015
materialsMaterials14.01.20.015
real_estateReal Estate35.00.90.008
utilitiesUtilities16.00.60.008
telecommunicationsTelecommunications14.00.80.01
transportationTransportation15.01.10.015

Gap 6 turns on this table: a perfectly balanced roster is what the realism numbers were measured on, and no real index looks like that.

## Instrument

Field

ticker · sectorName, and one of the twelve keys above.
initial_priceDay-zero price.
shares_outstandingShare count. With price, this gives market_cap.
epsEarnings per share, or None for a loss-maker, which is then valued off book value and never reprices on rates.
book_value_per_shareBalance-sheet value per share.
revenue_growthGrowth rate, fractional.
avg_volumeAverage daily volume. Held fixed through a run, and what participation is measured against.
betaLoading on the shared market factor.
short_interestA share count, not a fraction. Values strictly between 0 and 1 are refused for a company with a real share count, because that is what a fraction looks like and the mistake is otherwise silent.
market_capDerived, read-only.

## Macro

Field

vixVolatility level. Drives factor variance, spreads, correlation and credit spreads.
federal_funds_ratePolicy rate, fractional. Moves prices only at a meeting.
corporate_bond_yieldWhat equities discount off. None derives it from the policy rate and the spread.
inflation_rateFractional.
qe_pe_boostPolicy support for valuations.
fear_greed_indexSentiment, 0 to 100.
cycleBusiness-cycle phase: expansion, peak, contraction, trough or recovery.

## StrategySpec Grammar

A spec is a JSON document and SPEC_VERSION is currently 1. Adding a signal kind or a cadence extends the grammar without changing what existing specs mean, whereas changing what an existing kind ranks would be a new version.

JSON
Copy

```
{
"spec_version": 1,
"signal": {"kind": "momentum", "lookback_days": 1.0},
"portfolio": {"top_k": 5, "gross": 1.0},
"execution": {"max_participation": 0.02},
"cadence": "step"
}
```

Field

signal.kindOne of hold, random, momentum, mean_reversion, oracle, blend.
signal.lookback_daysOn momentum and mean_reversion. Days only, never steps, because a step is a harness artifact. Default 1.0.
signal.componentsOn blend: a list of {kind, weight, lookback_days?}. Blendable kinds are random, momentum, mean_reversion and oracle. Ranks combine first, then top_k selects from the blended ranking.
portfolio.top_kHow many names to hold. Applies to the ranked kinds only. Default 5.
portfolio.grossGross exposure. Default 1.0, or 0.5 for random.
execution.max_participationCap on any order as a fraction of average daily volume. Default 0.02, or 0.05 for hold.
cadence"step" re-decides at every decision point; "daily" only at each day's first step. hold must be "step".
seedRequired when the signal contains random, and refused otherwise.

oracle is privileged: it reads the true mispricing. It declares itself as such, which is why it is a reference rather than a competitor.

What the grammar cannot express: path dependence, conditional logic ("go flat if drawdown exceeds X"), custom signals, and anything reading engine internals except the oracle. Those need a Python agent, and such a result is reproducible by citing code at a commit rather than by a fingerprint.

## Exceptions

Nearly everything raises pt.ValidationError, with a message naming the specific thing that was wrong. These are the refusals worth knowing about in advance.

WhereWhat it refuses

envelope.checkA statistic name that is not a key of facts.REAL_MARKETS. A silently dropped name would be a silently granted certification.
envelope.intervalsFewer than two panels. A spread over one observation is not a spread.
atlas.axes_forA parameter that ships at zero and has no explicit range; a ranges or log key not in names; a duplicated name. It warns, rather than refusing, when a range excludes the preset's own value.
atlas.planFewer than 8 samples.
Survey.sensitivityFewer than 8 usable rows, or an output no row measured.
Survey.profileFewer than three rows per bin.
Survey.attributionA vector value outside the surveyed range (extrapolation), a parameter set on one side only, or a parameter that was not surveyed.
Survey.confirmAny seed shared with the survey or between blocks, and a survey with no seed record at all. An empty list is the absence of a record wearing the key.
ModelParams.from_presetAn override of a compile-time constant, by name. Accepting one the engine would ignore would make the fingerprint a lie.
ScenarioChaining a shape constructor onto a built scenario; a compare() baseline that realises the same path as the scenario.
RunManifest.reproduceA build whose arithmetic does not match the manifest's. It names the culprit rather than replaying a different market.
Checkpoint restoreA pre-split snapshot with three RNG numbers instead of nine, naming the era. It cannot be continued bit-exactly.
InstrumentA short_interest between 0 and 1 on a real share count, and an unknown sector key.
loss.band_distance_lossA missing or zero noise scale. An unweighted sum is a choice, and it will not make it by accident.

---


# Citing a Result

Source: https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/citing.html

REFERENCE

# Citing a Result

A citation identifies the software. It does not identify a run. A methods section needs both.

## Citing the Software

CITATION.cff at the repository root carries the metadata in Citation File Format. GitHub renders it as a "Cite this repository" button and reference managers read it directly.

There is no DOI yet. It is deliberately absent rather than invented: a Zenodo deposit mints one per release and one for the project as a whole, and that deposit is the next step. Until then, cite the version and the commit.

BIBTEX
Copy

```
@software{pretium,
author = {Coombes, Simon},
title = {pretium: a deterministic market simulator with a real
limit order book},
version = {0.3.0},
url = {https://github.com/simoncoombes/pretium},
note = {Commit . No DOI assigned; see CITATION.cff}
}
```

## Citing a Run

Seven things identify a market and what happened in it. Miss any one and the result cannot be rebuilt.

WhatWhy it is needed

package versionTrajectories change across versions. A figure from an earlier known-answer baseline is wrong by construction, not approximately right.
seedThe market. On its own it identifies nothing, because the same seed over a different roster is a different market.
universe fingerprintWhich roster, in which order. Tickers do not distinguish rosters, because they are generated positionally: random(40, seed=1) and random(40, seed=99) share every name and no fundamentals.
how the universe was builtThe fingerprint proves two rosters match; it does not let a reader construct yours. Give the constructor call, or ship the EDGAR snapshot.
macro initial conditionsDay zero, plus any scenario path or pin.
model fingerprintA preset name, or custom-XXXXXXXX. A custom model cannot present as a shipped one.
strategy fingerprintPresent when the strategy was a StrategySpec. Empty for a hand-written agent, which honestly says: cite code at a commit instead.

## Or Ship One File

RunManifest gathers all of it, fingerprints each part, and carries the expected result digest, so a reader is told whether they rebuilt the same market rather than eyeballing numbers.

PYTHON
Copy

```
import pretium as pt

universe = pt.Universe.random(40, seed=111)
spec = pt.StrategySpec.momentum(lookback_days=1.0, top_k=5)
engine = pt.Engine(seed=42, universe=universe)
engine.run_days(252)

manifest = pt.RunManifest.of(engine, seed=42, universe=universe,
strategy=spec)
open("run.json", "w").write(manifest.to_json())

# the reader, with the package and this file and nothing else:
same = pt.RunManifest.from_json(open("run.json").read()).reproduce()
```

reproduce() checks the build's arithmetic behaviourally before replaying, and refuses on any mismatch, naming what differs. A manifest that silently reproduced a different market would manufacture false confidence, which is worse than no manifest.

For a custom model the manifest embeds the full coefficient dictionary, so a modified market rebuilds bit for bit or is refused by name.

## Citing a Realism Claim

Do not quote the numbers on Realism and Limits for your own roster. Cite envelope.json, which carries the per-statistic detail, the gap list and the provenance, and re-measure the panel on your own universe with facts.measure if your roster is not sector-balanced. The determinism baseline for the current era is known-answer v11, digest 60d47572…0de590, which the release workflow checks inside every wheel before it uploads; every era boundary carries a different one, so a digest is an era marker rather than a version number. For the check that matters to a citation, compare pretium.model_preset()["name"] against the preset named in envelope.json: if they differ, the published page describes a different model than the one you are running.

## A Worked Methods Paragraph

Strategies were evaluated on pretium 0.3.0 (commit <sha>), model preset pt-v12, over a 40-instrument universe built with Universe.random(40, seed=111) (fingerprint 5d8de78b55aad752), simulation seeds 1 to 30, 252 trading days, default day-zero macro state and no scenario. The momentum strategy is StrategySpec.momentum(lookback_days=1.0, top_k=5), fingerprint <sha256>. Run manifests and order logs are archived at <location>. Realism of the shipped preset at this horizon is as published in envelope.json, which names the preset the figures describe; absolute returns are not claimed to forecast live results.

The last clause is not boilerplate. It is the one claim this simulator cannot support at any horizon or preset.

# Release Notes

Source: https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/releases.html

REFERENCE

# Release Notes

## Status - 0.3.0, current

Published on PyPI as pretium and on crates.io as the pretium crate. The API is exercised by the test suite and the example notebooks are executed rather than written and hoped over, so the code on this site runs. Published FIGURES are a separate discipline and a weaker guarantee: they are re-measured by tools/remeasure, which reports every number the stated method no longer produces, and a figure it flags is a documentation defect until someone corrects it. The API may move before 1.0. Each release is tagged and its wheels are built by the release workflow, which runs one fixed simulation inside every wheel and compares digests before anything is uploaded. There is no DOI yet.

- Rust core with a Python API. Wheels are abi3, CPython 3.11+, no Rust toolchain needed. The core package has no dependencies.

- Optional extras: pretium[rl] (numpy, gymnasium) and pretium[arrow] (pyarrow).

## 0.3.0 - current

pt-v12 is the default. It is the first preset that looks like a real market over two years as well as one.

| in band | pt-v10 | pt-v12 |
| one year | 14 of 14 | 14 of 14 |
| two years | 13 of 14 | 14 of 14 |
| a roster it never saw | 14 of 14 | 14 of 14 |

Thirty-seed medians. Only the two-year row moved, and it cost nothing on the other two rows.

Your numbers change if you did not name a preset. Every earlier preset still runs exactly as it did:

```
eng = pt.Engine(seed=42, universe=u, model="pt-v10")
```

The fix was one number. Volume stopped responding to a move at 4 percent, so a stock down 12 traded like a stock down 4. That cap had been in the engine since the first version and nobody chose it. It is now 12 percent.

One thing got worse. Under a real macro path, daily swings run 1.57x as wide as the real stock they are compared against, against 1.555x before. It is the scenario-magnitude gap.

pt-v11 also ships, and is not the default. It is the base pt-v12 is built on, and the first preset whose crises behave like real ones.

| in a crisis | pt-v10 | pt-v11 | real |
| volatility, calm to panic | 5.0x | 6.0x | 6.2x |
| how tightly names move together | 0.67 | 0.70 | 0.66 to 0.73 |
| how much industries hold together | +0.04 | +0.11 | +0.10 |

Two mechanisms did that. crisis_blend_gain was a fixed number, already at its maximum in any real crisis. So an earlier preset could only make a crisis more violent through company-specific movement, which pulled names apart. Companies also generate their own news now, and that news reaches their sector peers. Before this, one company's earnings surprise reached nobody.

Seventeen new settings, each at the value the engine already used, so no preset from pt-v1 to pt-v10 moves. ModelParams goes from 70 coefficients to 87. pt.ModelParams.settable() lists them.

The envelope covers more than it did. Six gaps become five. pt-v12 holds volume change in band at both horizons, so that gap is gone. Two-year and five-year runs are now measured rather than assumed. Over ten years, annualised volatility reads 31.5, 35.6, 30.2, 33.5, 33.0, 33.1, 31.3, 32.4, 32.4 and 31.6 percent, so nothing runs away and nothing drifts. The certified horizon stays 252 days, because the bands themselves were derived at one and two years. S&P-like, technology-heavy and defensive rosters all hold 14 of 14 at one year.

A bug fixed on the way. Driven a minute at a time, the model's own company news never reached you. A batched tick loop also rolled that news every minute. Both paths now print the same prices. This only affected pt-v11.

Documentation. Every published figure was re-measured against the engine. Three new pages: a glossary, the two loops, and the principles. References to the reference implementation no longer disclose its paths or its language, and tests/test_brand_commitments.py now fails if they come back.

## 0.2.0 - 2026-08-26

The default moved from pt-v3 to pt-v10, so the market itself is different. A run that names its preset replays exactly. A run that took the default does not.

pt-v10 is the first preset to hold all fourteen statistics in band at one year, and thirteen of fourteen at two years. The default before it held twelve and seven. That holds on training seeds, on new seeds, and on a 60-name universe it never saw.

| | pt-v3 | pt-v10 | real |
| days above its own crisis threshold | 0% | 10.2% | 12.5% |
| volatility, calm to panic | 3.07x | 5.05x | 6.16x |
| same-sector co-movement | 0.004 | 0.135 | 0.11 to 0.23 |

Correlation now has a memory, and volume behaves at one year. Volume change at two years is the one row of fourteen that still misses.

Two ground-truth defects fixed. A jump moved the mispricing state after the tick loop. So on a day a jump fired, the components did not sum to the move. A halted day booked its clamped price to nobody. truth() gains a jump column and a circuit_breaker column, Engine.FACTORS is nine, and the identity holds through a crisis to 1e-16. A decomposition published from 0.1.x is exact except on those days.

Snapshots now carry the log-volume state. A restored pt-v4 engine used to trade different volume and print different prices.

Two behaviour changes. A VIX pin acts on the first day, not the second. And order flow large enough to move the index now costs about as much through other names' volatility as through its own book.

Also: examples/00-a-year-in-one-market.ipynb, the entry point the examples were missing. Two envelope gaps closed, both recorded rather than dropped: two-year kurtosis moved from 5.23 to 8.26, and sector co-movement from 0.004 to 0.135. Three inflation constants became settings, measured against real CPI and taken by no preset.

## 0.1.4 - 2026-08-25

Two presets, four statistics, five settings. pt-v3 is still the default and pt-v1 through pt-v6 reproduce bit for bit.

pt-v7 is the first preset in which same-sector names co-move more than cross-sector names. pt-v8 is the first whose correlation has a memory: in this window correlation is the market factor's variance, and that variance had almost none. Both hold 13 of 14 in band at 504 days.

Four statistics join the panel: corr_asymmetry, corr_asymmetry_lagged, sector_excess_corr and corr_persistence_acf1. pt-v3 now reads 12 of 14 at 252 days and 7 of 14 at 504. The engine did not move. The misses were always there.

Five settings that were literals: crisis_blend_source, sector_vix_coupling, fair_value_book_floor, inflation_reversion and inflation_ceiling. Each ships at the value every preset already ran on.

New gap: the economy cannot reach its own crisis regimes. Endogenous inflation peaks near 4.1 percent, against a real CPI that reached 9.1 percent. So an inflation regime needs a scenario to drive it, and the gap says how. On real 2022 data over six seeds, against a real S&P of -20.0 percent:

| scenario | index |
| none | -12.6% |
| the real seven-hike path only | -13.1% |
| the published CPI path | -23.3% |

Inflation is the lever, because it steers the central bank into the corporate bond yield. A pinned policy rate does not.

What each macro field transmits. Measured by a shock on day 5, read on day 25.

| field | price move by day 25 |
| vix 15 to 60 | 39.2% |
| qe_pe_boost 0 to -0.30 | 38.3% |
| corporate_bond_yield 5.5% to 11.4% | 28.3% |
| federal_funds_rate 1.6% to 10% | 0.00% |
| inflation_rate 2% to 9% | 0.00% |
| fear_greed_index 50 to 0 | 0.00% |

Three fields act the day you move them. Two wait for a central bank meeting, because both work through the corporate bond yield. fear_greed_index is settable, validated, and read by no pricing code.

The real 2020-21 macro path now drives four scenario response channels rather than a claim. Every sign is right. Each channel runs at 70 to 85 percent of the size real AAPL shows, which is the scenario-magnitude gap from another angle.

## 0.1.3 - 2026-08-25

Two presets. pt-v3 is still the default, so nothing changes unless you ask for a preset by name.

pt-v6 holds 9 of 10 statistics at 252 days and 8 of 10 at 504, against 9 and 5 for pt-v3. It is not strictly better: the two tie at one year, and pt-v3 sits more comfortably inside six of the ten bands. What pt-v6 buys is tail room, from 0.80 to 7.20 seed standard deviations. Use it for multi-year work where the tail matters. pt-v3 is still the preset the envelope certifies.

A trade-off that was a wiring accident. pt-v4 reached the two-year tail and lost return_acf1 at one year. That looked like the price of the tail. It was one line. A jump moved the mispricing state after the momentum roll had read it. The next close then read the jump as a re-rating and continued it. jump_momentum_share separates the two. pt-v5 is pt-v4 with it at zero. pt-v6 also halves the herding term.

garch_beta_dispersion ships at zero. It was built for the decay-shape gap and moves away from it. The log-log slope reads -0.944 with it and -0.933 without, against a real -0.436. It is kept for a smaller gain it does give, on 504-day kurtosis and annualised volatility. Its documentation leads with the measurement, not with what it was for.

examples/09-a-pandemic-shaped-market.ipynb drives the real 2020-21 VIX, FOMC path and credit path through a 505-day run, and scores the result against Apple's shares. The daily series ship with it, so it runs offline. Two findings hold outside the notebook: only qe_pe_boost moves a valuation, and fear_greed_index moves nothing at all.

## 0.1.2 - 2026-08-24

Fixes the PyPI project page. The engine did not move.

The README linked to examples and licences by relative path. That works on GitHub and 404s on PyPI, which renders the same file. Eleven links were dead. It survived two releases because the file looks correct everywhere an author reads it. A test now fails on any relative README link. A second fails if an absolute link names a file that is not in the repository.

## 0.1.1 - 2026-08-24

A packaging fix. The engine did not move, so a result from 0.1.0 reproduces here exactly.

0.1.0 published five wheels and no source distribution. PyPI refused the sdist because it declared its licence files at the package root and the build had put them under rust/. The wheels were never affected, so the fault showed up on one artefact out of six. This release ships the sdist with the paths declared.

The v0.1.0 tag stays where it is. Moving it would break the link between that tag and the wheels published from it, and that link is the point.

## 0.1.0 - 2026-08-24

First release. pretium simulates an equity market you can run a strategy against. It runs prices, a limit order book with price-time priority and partial fills, and an economy that advances each day. Orders match against real depth, so your trades move the price.

On top of that sit agent evaluation, ranking across seeds with paired sign tests, transaction cost analysis, sweeps and replay. There are also checkpoints with branching, a Gymnasium environment, five Arrow tables, and an SEC EDGAR loader.

Two things are less usual. The simulator computed every price, so it can tell you why one moved. That is seven factor contributions per instrument per tick, and they sum to the move. The same seed also gives the same market. So you can run it twice, once with your orders and once without, and price every fill against the market where you never traded.

Determinism. Five targets build a wheel, run one fixed simulation inside it, and compare digests. Verified on linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, macos-arm64, macos-x86_64 and windows-x86_64, all reproducing

```
5bd011be292f823ce1c360d1a12bf46de3362deee058a37283c74ab47069d0c1
```

A WebAssembly build gives the same numbers, so the engine can run in a browser without becoming a second model.

Realism. Ten statistics are measured against real-market bands. At 252 days pt-v3 holds nine of ten, and holds the same nine on seeds and a roster the calibration never saw. The tenth is the autocorrelation of volume changes, which misses by 13.7 seed standard deviations. It is outside the calibration objective on purpose: an optimiser pointed at a target it cannot reach distorts everything else. Six further gaps say what each one stops you concluding, and envelope.check() refuses a question that falls outside them.

pt-v4 also ships and is not the default. It is the first preset to bring 504-day kurtosis inside its band, and it pays at one year, holding eight of ten.

Versioning. Anything that changes the simulated trajectory is a breaking change here, however small. A market that runs differently from the same seed invalidates every published result that cited it. So coefficient changes arrive as a new preset, and old presets keep running as they did.

## Known-answer v8 - 2026-08, era boundary

Every seeded trajectory changed. Runs from before this baseline are not comparable to runs after it. Figures below are the six-seed panel method (Universe.random(40, seed=111), sim seeds 1 to 6, 252 days), which is what pt.facts reports. The 30-seed certification panel on Realism and Limits measures the same statistics on a different roster draw and horizon sample, and the two are not interchangeable: the leverage effect reads −0.085 here against −0.0349 certified, and volume against absolute return +0.585 against +0.5339. Quote whichever method you actually ran.

- The macro chain now advances from Python. VIX steps daily, policy fields step at the central bank's meeting calendar, fair value reprices when the discount rate moves. Previously every field held its initial value for the whole run.

- The shared market factor got its own conditional variance process, coupled to VIX. Cross-sectional correlation moved from +0.024 to +0.257; a pinned VIX 45 takes it to +0.68.

- Added a GJR asymmetry term, which produces the leverage effect. Now reads -0.085, negative on six seeds of six.

- Removed the average-volume feedback that compounded the volume level. Volume against absolute return moved from +0.105 to +0.585.

- Split the RNG into three streams (market, economy, external), so TCA counterfactuals are exact and host randomness cannot shift a market.

- Re-derived the realism bands with provenance. Verdicts moved in both directions: on the six-seed method lag-one clustering came out above its re-derived band, and the leverage effect came inside one. On the 30-seed certification panel lag-one clustering reads +0.1413 and is inside the band, which is the number the shipped certificate carries: the two methods disagree on this row, and that disagreement is the point of naming the method.

- Added presets pt-v2 and pt-v3. pt-v3 is now the default.

- Fixed model_preset() reporting pt-v1 after the engine default became pt-v3. No simulated value changed; the known-answer digest moved, because it hashes the reported preset.

- Fixed the GARCH process being fed the day's total return instead of its noise component. Clustering fell from +0.12 to +0.10; the fix stayed, because it is what the model specifies.

- Corrected the RNG parity claim. The integer core is bit-identical to the reference; normal draws differ on 1.545% of 60,000 recorded draws, first divergence at draw 12.

## Known-answer v5 - commit ad91026

- Determinism gate run across all five targets (Linux x86_64 and aarch64, macOS arm64 and x86_64, Windows x86_64). Identical digests, each also passing against the committed baseline.

## Known-answer v3 - commit a5afd1c

- Determinism gate run on Windows x86_64 and macOS arm64. Identical digests.

## Checking Your Build

PYTHON
Copy

```
import pretium as pt

pt.__version__ # package version
pt.model_preset()["name"] # coefficient set in use
```

# Core Types

Source: https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/api-core.html

API

# Core Types

## Engine

Engine(seed, universe, macro_state=None, model=None)A market. model is a preset name or a ModelParams; the default is pt-v12.
run_days(n)Advance n trading days. The macro chain steps at every close.
bars(grain="day")OHLCV as Arrow. Two grains, "tick" and "day", plus minutes=N to bucket ticks into bars of that many minutes. Any other grain raises, and grain and minutes cannot both be passed.
truth()One row per instrument per tick: fundamental value, anchor price, mispricing, and nine factor contributions that sum to the move.
pin_macro(**fields)Override the endogenous chain for a field from today onward.
draw_uniform() · draw_normal()Host randomness from the external stream. Never touches the market's sequence.
draws_by_stream()Per-stream draw counts: market, economy, external.
model_fingerprintThe preset's name, or custom-XXXXXXXX. Never both.
state_snapshot()Serialisable engine state, RNG streams included, for Checkpoint.

## Universe, Instrument, Macro

Universe.random(n, seed)Generated roster, plausible fundamentals. Sectors are handed out round-robin over the twelve, so each holds n/12 names give or take one: the certified 40-name roster puts four in four sectors and three in the other eight, and only n=60 gives five each. The universe seed is a separate input domain from the simulation seed.
Universe([Instrument, ...])Explicit roster. A list subclass, and order is contractual: a re-sorted universe is a different market.
Universe.from_edgar(snapshot)Real fundamentals from SEC EDGAR.
universe.fingerprintsha256 over the canonical roster, order included.
Instrument(ticker, sector, initial_price, ...)Fundamentals: shares outstanding, eps, book value, revenue growth, average volume, beta, short interest.
Macro(federal_funds_rate, corporate_bond_yield, vix, ...)Day-zero macro state. Rates are fractional: 0.025 is 2.5%.

## ModelParams

ModelParams.from_preset(name, **overrides)A coefficient set. Bit-identical to a shipped preset fingerprints as that preset's name; anything else as custom-XXXXXXXX. Immutable once built.
settable()The runtime-settable surface. Non-settable constants are refused by name.
to_dict() · fingerprintThe full surface, and the hash over it.
model_preset()The compact coefficient table the determinism gate digests.

## Scenario: Events and Crises

Scenario().hold(**fields)Pin macro fields at a level: a held VIX 45 is a sustained crisis.
Scenario().ramp(field, start=, end=, over=)Walk a field over a window: an inflation shock, a hiking cycle.
Scenario().step(field, before=, after=, at=)Jump a field on a given day. Pins on one field lie end to end, so spike, plateau and decay compose into one scenario.
Scenario.rate_shock(...) · vix_shock(...) · vol_shock(...)Shape constructors: each builds a whole event in one call.
scenario.table(days) · to_json(days) · from_json(text)Inspect the day-by-day path before spending a run on it; serialise it so a result can cite the exact event.
engine.pin_macro(**fields)The same override, applied directly mid-run. Logged, so the run still replays.

evaluate, tca.analyse, facts.measure and run_many all take scenario=. The guide chapter is Scenarios and crises.

## Identity and Reproduction

StrategySpec.momentum(lookback_days, top_k)A strategy as a declarative, versioned, hashable document. A hand-written agent still works; its fingerprint is empty rather than fake.
RunManifest.of(engine, seed, universe, strategy)One shareable document embedding every component with its fingerprint and the expected result digest.
manifest.reproduce()Checks the build's arithmetic behaviourally, replays, and on any mismatch refuses, naming the culprit.
Checkpoint · branch(...)Freeze a market mid-run; fork two futures from an identical state.
GameRng(seed, sequence)The PCG32 generator itself. Public, raw, and the replay surface for pre-split recordings.

---


# Running and Evaluating

Source: https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/api-run.html

API

# Running and Evaluating

The evaluation harness and what surrounds it: agents, scoring, ranking across seeds, scenarios, execution analysis and the RL environment.

## Evaluation

evaluate(agents, seed, universe, days, scenario=None, model=None)Score a dict of agents or StrategySpecs on one market. Returns Scorecards carrying seed, universe, model and strategy fingerprints.
rank(factory, seeds, universe, days, workers)The same tournament across many seeded markets, in parallel.
ranking.separation(a, b)Wins minus losses and a sign-test p, paired across markets. The guard against crowning a one-seed leader.
reference_agents(seed)The built-in baselines: momentum, mean reversion and friends.
capture_ratio(scorecard, oracle)A module-level function, not a Scorecard field: return earned against what the oracle says was available. Prefer it to raw percentages.
sweep(...) · replay(log, ...)Streamed multi-seed runs; drive a recorded order log by hand.

## Scenarios

Scenario.rate_shock(start, end, over)Walk rates across a window while the strategy holds positions.
run_scenario(...)Run one scenario directly.

Scenario response is directional, and its magnitude is a named gap: use scenarios to detect breakage, never to size it. See Realism and limits.

## Execution Analysis

tca.analyse(algo, seed, universe, days)Runs your algorithm, re-runs the identical market without your orders, and prices every fill against the untraded world.
Execution.shortfall_bps()What your footprint cost, in basis points.
Execution.by_step()Where you paid it.
Execution.partial_fills()What you asked for versus what you got.

## Reinforcement Learning

pretium.gym.TradingEnv(universe, seed, days)A gymnasium environment. Actions are target weights in [-1, 1]; reward is measured after the market moves, so it includes the agent's own footprint. Passes env_checker.

# Realism and Atlas

Source: https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/api-realism.html

API

# Realism and Atlas

Measuring what the market reproduces, pricing what it does not, and mapping what it responds to.

## pretium.facts

measure(seed=, universe=, days=252,        macro=None, scenario=None,        model=None)Run a market and report the fourteen-statistic panel. Carries model and universe fingerprints. A statistic that cannot be measured comes back None, never zero.
REAL_MARKETS · SEED_SDThe real-market bands with provenance, and each statistic's across-seed noise at the shipped baseline.
band_distance(value, low, high)Zero inside the band, distance to the nearer edge outside.
compare_to_real_markets(facts) · report(facts)Per-statistic verdicts, as data and as a printed table. Refuses to aggregate into one score.

## pretium.loss

### What each of the fourteen does in the loss

Each statistic has one of three roles, and the roles are one tuple
each in pretium.loss. The third is
derived as the complement of the first two, so promoting a statistic is a
one-tuple edit and a statistic added to
facts.REAL_MARKETS is excluded and
reported by default rather than silently optimised against.

rolemembers
what the role means

live target5 of 14
annualised_vol_pctreturn_acf1abs_return_acf1abs_return_acf5cross_sectional_corrIn the loss with a band and a weight. The search moves these.constraint4 of 14
excess_kurtosisvolume_abs_return_corrleverage_effectabs_return_acf20Measured and penalised outside its band, so an optimiser cannot break it for free.structural5 of 14
volume_change_acf1corr_asymmetrycorr_asymmetry_laggedsector_excess_corrcorr_persistence_acf1Zero weight in the objective. Membership describes the objective rather than reachability: the shipped preset holds all five in band at the certified horizon.

band_distance_loss(panel, seed_sd=None, bands=None)L_real: squared band distances in units of each statistic's own seed noise, summed over the live set. Returns the breakdown with the scalar inside it, never a bare float.
seed_sd_from_panels(panels)Across-seed standard deviation per statistic, from per-seed panels.
LIVE_TARGETS · CONSTRAINTS · STRUCTURALLoss membership as data: five targets, four constraints, and the five STRUCTURAL statistics reported in every result and excluded from the objective. Membership is about the objective, not about reachability: two of those five, volume_change_acf1 and sector_excess_corr, were called structurally unreachable until 0.2.0 and the shipped preset holds both in band at the certified horizon.

## pretium.envelope

check(horizon_days=, statistics=(),      sector_concentrated=False,      scenario_magnitude=False)Can this market answer the question? Returns a Verdict, falsy when outside, every reason naming its measurement. Unknown statistic names raise.
intervals(panels) · report_intervals(rows)Per-statistic spread across seeds beside median and band. Refuses fewer than two panels: a spread over one observation is not a spread.
score(panel, horizon_days=)A measured panel against the bands for its own horizon, with room_sd per statistic. Guards against scoring one horizon with another's ruler.
regressions(panel)Statistics the shipped preset holds in band and this panel does not. Empty means no regression against what ships.
GAPS · certified()The five measured gaps with what each forbids, and the whole list as a plain mapping for a manifest.
CERTIFIED_HORIZON_DAYS · PRESET252, and pt-v12. If your installed preset differs, check() says so rather than answering.

## pretium.atlas

axes_for(names, preset="pt-v3", ranges=None, log=())Axes around shipped values. Refuses zero-shipped parameters without an explicit range, and typo'd override names.
plan(axes, samples, seed)The vectors a survey would measure, before spending anything.
survey(axes, measure, samples)Measure every planned vector. Errors are recorded rather than fatal.
Survey.sensitivity · profile · unidentified · pareto · attribution · explain · report_front · confirmThe analysis surface. Every numeric result carries its row counts and drop tally. See the Atlas reference.
Survey.save(path) · load(path) · provenance()Measure once, ask many questions later, and what the map stands on.

# Model Parameters

Source: https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/api-params.html

API

# Model Parameters

What each model coefficient controls. This page explains the 58 coefficients that most often get changed; pt.ModelParams.settable() is the complete list and returns all 90 from your installed wheel, up from 70 at 0.2.0.

Two rules hold everywhere. Nothing settable changes how many random draws happen or in what order, so two coefficient sets on one seed see identical noise and every difference in the outcome is a parameter effect. And several newer mechanisms ship at 0.0, where the code skips the branch entirely, so earlier presets reproduce bit for bit.

## The Shared Factors

Every return has three parts: a move the whole market shares, a move the sector shares, and the name's own private noise. These set the size of each part.

market_factor_sigmaHow big the shared market-wide move is on a normal day. Every stock feels this one.
sector_factor_sigmaThe same, for each sector's shared move.
idio_sigma_scaleScales each name's own private volatility. 1.0 leaves it untouched. pt-v3 pays for a bigger market factor by setting this to 0.84.

## Order Flow and News

order_flow_coefficientHow hard aggregate order flow pushes the price.
informed_flow_fractionThe share of that push that sticks. The rest fades back.
news_sector_weight · news_market_weightHow much sector-wide and market-wide news events move each name.
news_peer_weight · news_peer_weight_downHow much one company's news moves its sector peers. At 0.0 an earnings beat moves only the company that reported it. Bad news gets its own knob because it spreads harder than good news in real markets.

## Per-Name Volatility: GJR-GARCH

The recipe behind volatility clustering: a big move today makes a big move tomorrow more likely. Each name runs its own copy.

garch_omegaThe base level variance returns toward.
garch_alphaHow much yesterday's shock raises today's variance. Bigger alpha, jumpier volatility.
garch_betaHow much of yesterday's variance carries over. Bigger beta, longer memory.
garch_gammaThe extra kick after a down day. This is where the leverage effect comes from. Zero gives plain symmetric GARCH, bit for bit.
garch_ceiling_multiple · garch_floor_multipleBounds on the variance, as multiples of the sector's long-run level. The ceiling binds on clustering, so it is searched under bounds.

## The Market Factor's Variance

The shared factor has its own variance process, and VIX steers it. This is why crisis volatility and crisis correlation arrive together.

market_vol_alpha · market_vol_betaShock take-up and persistence. pt-v3 runs the persistence at 0.989 to buy clustering, and that one choice is what weakened the crisis transient (gap 5).
market_vol_vix_couplingHow much the variance target follows VIX. 0 ignores it; 1 makes the target proportional to VIX².
market_vol_vix_anchorThe VIX level where the coupled target equals baseline. Ships at 15, so an average VIX reproduces the uncoupled process exactly.
market_vol_ceiling_multiple · market_vol_floor_multipleClamps on the factor variance. pt-v12 ships the ceiling at 32x baseline where pt-v3 had 8x, which is a physical number rather than a fitted one: a real record VIX of 82.7 against this model's anchor of 15 is a variance ratio of 30, and anything lower stops the market reaching the variance a real record implies. With the shipped VIX coupling the clamp binds around VIX 87, where on pt-v3's 8x it bound around 43.
market_vol_slow_persistence · market_vol_slow_gain · market_vol_slow_weightA second, slower variance component: the fast one chases spikes, this one carries long-horizon clustering. All three at 0.0 recover the single-component process bit for bit.
market_vol_slow_vix_dampDecouples the slow component from VIX. Measured, and the measurement refuted the idea behind it: damping makes both the shock response and the steady-state lever worse at every setting tried. Ships inert.

## Crisis Behaviour

crisis_vix_thresholdThe VIX level where crisis behaviour switches on: the correlation blend, the stress memory, the economy's crisis premium. Ships at 25.5, the 94th percentile of the endogenous VIX distribution, chosen so the trigger can actually fire.
crisis_blend_ramp · crisis_blend_capHow many VIX points past the threshold before correlations top out, and where the ceiling sits.
crash_amplifier_threshold · crash_amplifier_slopeHow big a market shock has to be (in normal-day units) before every name loads harder on the market, and how much harder per extra unit.
universe_stress_decay · universe_stress_weightFear memory. Without it, correlations decouple the same tick VIX dips back under the threshold. With it, stress ratchets up instantly and fades over weeks, the way real crisis correlation does.
regime_stress_pointsStress the business cycle feeds into that same memory, in VIX-equivalent points. At 0.0 the price process behaves as though the economy were always expanding.
vix_mean_reversionHow fast VIX falls back toward its target each day. The other half of the transient problem: a longer spike stresses the market without touching variance persistence.

## Jumps

Without jumps, prices only diffuse, and nothing ever gaps. That is why 504-day kurtosis read 5.2 against a real 7.1 to 22 on pt-v3, the last preset with both jump intensities at zero, so no jump ever fired: fat tails at that scale need surprises. With them live the shipped pt-v12 reads 7.7528 there, inside the band. Jumps draw from their own RNG stream, so a preset with them off is bit-identical to one that predates them.

jump_intensity_market · jump_sigma_marketDaily probability and size of a market-wide jump.
jump_mean_marketNegative on purpose: real crash jumps point down. A symmetric jump would fix kurtosis on the panel while getting crises backwards.
jump_intensity_idio · jump_sigma_idioPer-name jumps, independent across names: the earnings-surprise channel.

## Volume

volume_variance_gainHow strongly realised volume tracks the market factor's variance, so busy prices come with busy volume.
volume_persistence · volume_innovation_sigmaA shared day-to-day volume process, so a busy day is followed by a busy day. This is the machinery that made volume_change_acf1 reachable: without a volume process, day-to-day volume changes are pure noise and their autocorrelation sits near −0.5 at any coefficients. It was called structurally unreachable until 0.2.0 and it is not. pt-v12 reads −0.2656 at 252 days against a band of −0.32 to −0.20 and −0.2572 at 504 against −0.29 to −0.21, and the gap that named it is retired.
volume_move_response · volume_move_cap · volume_move_floor · volume_move_noiseHow much more a name trades per one percent it has moved today, where that response saturates, the baseline it sits on, and the return-unrelated noise around it. The cap is the whole of pt-v12: at the 4.0 every preset from pt-v1 to pt-v11 shipped, a name that fell twelve percent traded exactly as much as one that fell four, so every crisis session was pinned to one value and contributed no covariance at all. Raising it to 12.0, roughly where a real exchange starts halting, took the 504-day panel from 13/14 in band to 14/14 and the held-out universe from 13/14 to 14/14, and cost nothing else measured.

## Size Effects

Small companies are more volatile and cost more to trade. The original model did this in four hard steps, which put cliffs in the cross-section: a $49B company and a $51B company differed by 25% in volatility. These blend the steps into smooth curves.

size_effect_smoothness · size_effect_exponentBlend from the four-tier volatility step toward a continuous power law (0 = steps, 1 = pure curve), and the curve's slope. The exponent ships at 0.15, fitted to the steps where the steps make sense.
spread_size_smoothness · spread_size_exponentThe same for the bid-ask spread, where the steps were worse: 10 bps at $1.0B, 30 bps at $0.9B. The exponent ships at 0.455, fitted the same way.

## Mispricing Dynamics

The wedge between price and true value: how far it stretches, how fast it heals, and how much the crowd chases it. This is the layer the truth table records.

mispricing_half_life_daysTrading days for half a mispricing to fade. The one knob for the decay: setting it recomputes the two derived values below.
mispricing_phi · s_phi_tickDerived from the half-life (daily and per-tick decay). Carried as recorded bit patterns; you cannot set them directly.
momentum_thetaHerding: the fraction of yesterday's re-rating that continues today. The knob behind trending returns. At pt-v1’s 0.25 it measures +0.249 at lag one; pt-v3 ships 0.0742 and measures +0.0375, inside the real band of −0.08 to 0.06. A counterfactual at 0.05 measured +0.034 on an earlier model era.
crowd_valuation_gain · crowd_momentum_gainHow hard the crowd leans on cheapness and on yesterday's move.

## Guards

Worst-case guarantees. Settable, so you can study them, and excluded from any calibration search, because a guard tuned for realism stops being a guarantee.

mispricing_capHard bound on how far price can stretch from value.
crowd_lean_capBound on the crowd's daily push.
price_breaker_fractionThe circuit-breaker band around the session open. Ships at ±25%.
price_hard_capAbsolute cap on any model price. Ships at 50,000.

To find out which of these move an outcome you care about, and by how much, survey them with Atlas before you turn anything. To set one: pt.ModelParams.from_preset("pt-v3", garch_alpha=0.12), which fingerprints as custom. The rest of the preset surface (fair-value coefficients, the macro chain's constants, the book geometry) is visible in to_dict() and refused by name if you try to set it, because those constants are compiled in and a silently ignored override would make the fingerprint a lie.

---


# Shipped Presets

Source: https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/api-presets.html

API

# Shipped Presets

A preset is a complete, named, frozen set of model coefficients. Name one when you build an engine, or pass nothing and get the default.

PYTHON
Copy

```
eng = pt.Engine(seed=42, universe=u) # pt-v12, the default
eng = pt.Engine(seed=42, universe=u, model="pt-v12") # the same, spelled out
eng = pt.Engine(seed=42, universe=u, model="pt-v1") # an earlier era, still exact
eng = pt.Engine(seed=42, universe=u, model="pt-v4") # for multi-year questions
```

## The Shipped Presets

pt-v1The original reference model, ported from the engine this library grew out of. Herding runs strong (momentum_theta 0.25), which is what made momentum so profitable in early eras. Kept selectable and bit-reproducing forever, so old results stay checkable.
pt-v2The first calibrated preset, produced by the calibration tooling against the re-derived realism bands. Selectable, never the default. Its certificate and report are committed in the repository.
pt-v3The default until pt-v10 replaced it at 0.2.0, produced the same way, and the preset the realism numbers described then: nine of the ten statistics measured at the time were in band at 252 days. Herding is turned well down (momentum_theta 0.0742).
pt-v4Selectable, and deliberately not the default. pt-v3 plus nine parameters that ship inert on pt-v3: five endogenous jump coefficients, three volume-process parameters, and market_factor_sigma. Built to investigate horizons past a year, which is not the same as being certified for them: nothing in this project is certified past 252 days.

## Choosing Between pt-v3 and pt-v4

A historical choice, kept because work published against either preset still reproduces. Neither is the default: pt-v12 has been since 2026-08-26, and it holds all fourteen statistics at 252 days AND all fourteen at 504, so it dominates both rows below. The full table of the twelve shipped presets is on Presets and Custom Models.

The two counts below are out of the ten-statistic panel of the pt-v3 era, and the two horizons disagree.

Horizonpt-v3pt-v4

252 days (certified)9/10 in band8/10
504 days5/107/10

Between these two, and only these two: pt-v3 at or under a year, pt-v4 for INVESTIGATING longer horizons. Neither licenses a multi-year backtest, which the realism page forbids on every preset, and pt-v12 beats both at both horizons.

What pt-v4 buys is the thin-tails gap, which nothing before it had moved: excess kurtosis at 504 days goes from 5.23 to 9.19, inside the horizon-matched band of 7.1 to 22. It halves the dual-horizon objective, 0.9887 to 0.4863 on training seeds and 1.3990 to 0.7493 on thirty seeds the search never saw.

What it costs is return_acf1 at the certified horizon: 0.0739 on training seeds, 0.0838 on held-out seeds, and 0.0801 on a held-out 60-name universe, against a band ceiling of 0.06. Three independent axes agreeing makes that a regression rather than seed noise.

That is why it is not the default. Promoting it would turn the envelope's nine-of-ten into eight-of-ten, and the statistic it gives up is the one behind "momentum works here for the wrong reason", which is the defect pt-v3 exists to have fixed.

## Why Presets Exist

So results can be compared. Package version, model, universe fingerprint and seed pin a market down completely, so two papers quoting pt-v3 ran the same coefficients to the bit. If everyone ran their own, "tested on the pretium simulator" would mean nothing. Presets never change once shipped. A recalibration gets a new name, and the old names keep producing exactly what they always did.

## Reading a Preset

pt.model_preset()The compact coefficient table for the default, in its exact historical shape. The cross-platform determinism gate hashes every value in it.
ModelParams.from_preset(name)The full surface as an object: read any coefficient, or override some and get an honestly named custom model.
engine.model_fingerprintWhat the engine is actually running: a preset's name, or custom-XXXXXXXX. A modified set can never present as a shipped preset, and a set bit-identical to a preset fingerprints as the preset.

The workflow for changing coefficients, and why the fingerprint rule exists, is the guide chapter Presets and custom models. What each coefficient does is Model parameters.

---
